title: Impact of IPO Lockup Expiry on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event–study design.  
Why: IPO-lockup expiration dates are known in advance and occur at (almost) different calendar times for each firm, providing a plausibly exogenous shock to the float of outstanding shares. The event-study framework isolates abnormal returns (AR) attributable to that single, well-defined event and cumulates them into CAR.  
Key assumptions  
• Market-model validity: E(AR)=0 in the absence of the event (ret = α+β·mkt_ret+ε).  
• No confounding firm-specific news in the narrow event window.  
• Non-overlapping events make cross-sectional averaging unbiased and independent.  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# IPO-Lockup Expiry Event Study – Complete, Reproducible Code
############################################################
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s57_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 stock_id = col_integer(),
                 event_day = col_integer(),
                 ret = col_double(),
                 mkt_ret = col_double(),
                 beta = col_double())
               )

# 2. Construct abnormal returns using provided betas -----------------------
df <- df %>% mutate(AR = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# 3. Average abnormal return (AAR) by relative day -------------------------
aar <- df %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(AAR = mean(AR),
            SE  = sd(AR)/sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(t_stat = AAR/SE)

cat("\nAverage Abnormal Returns by Event Day\n")
print(aar, n = Inf)

# 4. Cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around the event ---------------------
# Main window: [-1, +1]
car_main <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1, event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

main_res <- car_main %>%
  summarise(mean_CAR = mean(CAR),
            sd_CAR   = sd(CAR),
            n        = n(),
            t_stat   = mean_CAR / (sd_CAR / sqrt(n)))

cat("\nMain CAR (-1,+1) across 80 IPOs\n")
print(main_res)

# 5. Regression-based robustness (difference-in-differences flavour) -------
# Pre-window: [-5,-1]  Post-window: [0,+5]
df_reg <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -5, event_day <= 5) %>%
  mutate(Post = if_else(event_day >= 0, 1, 0))

reg <- lm(AR ~ Post + mkt_ret, data = df_reg)   # controlling for market return
cat("\nOLS of AR on Post indicator (-5..+5 window)\n")
print(tidy(reg))

# 6. Alternative CAR window robustness -------------------------------------
# Alternative window: [-3, +3]
car_alt <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -3, event_day <= 3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(mean_CAR = mean(CAR),
            sd_CAR   = sd(CAR),
            n        = n(),
            t_stat   = mean_CAR / (sd_CAR / sqrt(n)))

cat("\nRobustness CAR (-3,+3) across 80 IPOs\n")
print(car_alt)

# 7. Very conservative abnormal return: AR2 = ret − mkt_ret ----------------
df <- df %>% mutate(AR2 = ret - mkt_ret)
car_alt2 <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1, event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR2 = sum(AR2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(mean_CAR = mean(CAR2),
            sd_CAR   = sd(CAR2),
            n        = n(),
            t_stat   = mean_CAR / (sd_CAR / sqrt(n)))

cat("\nRobustness CAR using naïve AR (beta=1), (-1,+1)\n")
print(car_alt2)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. When restricted insiders can finally sell, the sudden increase in free float is expected to put downward pressure on prices.  
Magnitude: Empirically, prior literature reports roughly –2 % to –5 % CAR over the (-1,+1) window. Given typical small-cap IPO betas and market reactions, I expect the mean CAR in this sample to fall around –3 % (-0.03), statistically different from zero at the 1 % level.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR before and after lockup expiry.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The lockup expiry leads to a negative impact on CAR.
